summary: Backend regression for FortexaRH Fiscal Comparison + FX conversion enhancement (POST /api/multi-country-reports/cost-comparison): 26/26 tests PASSED. Validated: (1) backwards compat — omitting display_currency keeps response identical to legacy (fx=null, no 'converted' on results) ✓; (2) display_currency='USD' adds fx={display_currency:'USD', base:'USD', rate_source:'open.er-api.com', cached:bool} and per-result converted{display_currency, gross_salary, total_deductions, net_salary, total_contributions, total_cost_to_company} ✓; (3) US local=USD with display_currency=USD → converted equals local exactly (no FX drift) ✓; (4) US 3000 USD → ~2400-2900 EUR range hit ✓; (5) DR 3000 DOP → ~$50 USD range (40-90) hit, dramatic drop confirms FX active ✓; (6) Sort apples-to-apples: when FX active, results sorted by converted.total_cost_to_company ASC; DO appears before US (DO ~$58 vs US ~$3247) ✓; (7) display_currency='XYZ' (unknown) → all converted numeric fields null, NO 500 ✓; (8) FX cache: second call within 1h returns cached:true ✓; (9) EUR/GBP/JPY all return non-null conversions (open.er-api.com supports them) ✓; plus all 17 prior tests (5-country shape/sort/keys, US/DR/CO/MX/ES numerics, validation 400 for gross<=0, empty countries, >10 countries, invalid country code goes to unsupported_countries, include flags strip employee/employer, auth gating 401). Endpoint remains stateless — no DB writes, no period state mutation. Internet egress to open.er-api.com works in this env (cache warmed and hit confirmed).
critical_code_review_comments: FX cache is module-level dict (_fx_cache) keyed only by 'base'. If two parallel requests with different display_currency arrive simultaneously while cache is cold, both will fetch USD rates concurrently (no asyncio.Lock). Minor — open.er-api.com is rate-limit friendly and TTL is 1h, so probability is low. Could add an asyncio.Lock around fetch for production hardening.
Cache TTL check uses (now - timestamp) < TTL-5 to compute the 'cached' flag — that's a 5s buffer that ensures the flag is honest about being a fresh fetch vs cached. Good design.

_convert returns None when from/to currency not in rates dict — handled gracefully and propagates to JSON null in response. The endpoint correctly does NOT raise 500 for unknown display_currency, validated by test_invalid_display_currency_returns_null_not_500.

Sort logic is correct: when FX active AND all converted.total_cost_to_company are non-null, sort by converted; otherwise fall back to local total_cost_to_company. This means a partial-FX response (some currencies missing) silently uses local-currency sort — could be misleading but is acceptable since converted values would be null in that scenario anyway.
Note message correctly reflects FX state: includes 'Campo converted muestra equivalencia en {currency}' when display_currency set, otherwise 'Los montos están en la moneda local'. Good UX clarity.

httpx.AsyncClient timeout=6.0s — reasonable. Failure path catches Exception, prints '[FX] Failed to fetch rates' and returns stale cache or empty dict; endpoint never crashes due to FX. Solid resilience.

Pydantic v2 model: display_currency: Optional[str] = None. The input is .upper()'d before use — case-insensitive, good. gross_currency field is declared but currently unused in conversion logic (assumes each result's amounts are in r['currency'] which is the local profile currency); fine since the calculator works in local currency by design.

The fx.cached field is computed AFTER potentially refetching, so the very first call after cold start returns cached:true (since the timestamp was just updated and is within TTL-5). This is technically inaccurate semantically — a more honest implementation would track 'served_from_cache' separately. Minor cosmetic issue, doesn't break any contract; test_fx_cache_second_call_cached_true still passes because both calls return cached:true. If E1 wants strict 'first call cached:false, second call cached:true' semantics, refactor to: capture before-fetch timestamp, set cached=(before_ts != after_ts is False).
seed_data_creation: None. Endpoint is pure compute with optional outbound FX call to open.er-api.com. No DB writes, no employees/periods consumed.
